examData.text: Which of the following best describes a computer network?
options: A collection of computers that operate independently and store information separately without communicating with one another.
A collection of two or more computers and other digital devices connected together to communicate and share data, resources, and services.
A group of computer programs installed on a single computer to perform different tasks without requiring additional hardware.
A collection of electronic devices connected only to a common power source so that they can operate simultaneously.

examData.text: A school connects 30 computers to a common network so that students can exchange files, communicate with one another, and use the same printer. What is the main purpose of this arrangement?
options: To ensure that each computer operates independently without depending on any other computer in the laboratory.
To allow every computer to function as a central server that permanently stores all information belonging to the school.
To enable communication and resource sharing among connected computers, thereby improving efficiency and reducing unnecessary duplication.
To eliminate the need for operating systems and application software on the computers connected to the network.

examData.text: Which component of a computer network enables a computer or another digital device to establish a network connection?
options: A Network Interface Card (NIC), which provides wired Ethernet or wireless connectivity to the network.
A Central Processing Unit (CPU), which directs network traffic between different geographical networks.
A Random Access Memory (RAM), which converts electrical signals into wireless communication signals.
A Read Only Memory (ROM), which connects computers to shared printers and determines the destination of network packets.

examData.text: Which statement correctly describes network transmission media?
options: They are software programs that control how users access files stored on a central server.
They are hardware devices responsible for assigning passwords to computers before they can join a network.
They are the channels through which data travels between connected devices, including wired cables and wireless signals.
They are storage devices used to retain information after the computers in a network have been switched off.

examData.text: Which of the following is a correct classification of the basic components of a computer network?
options: Computers and devices, network interface cards, transmission media, network devices, and network software.
Word processors, spreadsheets, presentation slides, databases, and desktop publishing applications.
Input devices, output devices, printing devices, calculation devices, and entertainment devices only.
Operating systems, programming languages, computer games, graphic designs, and document formatting tools.

examData.text: A student connects a smartphone to wireless earbuds and a smartwatch to exchange data over short distances. Which type of network is being used?
options: A Metropolitan Area Network because several electronic devices communicate with one another.
A Wide Area Network because the connected devices can exchange digital information.
A Local Area Network because the devices are connected within a relatively small geographical area.
A Personal Area Network because it connects personal devices around an individual over a short distance.

examData.text: Which situation is the best example of a Local Area Network (LAN)?
options: A network connecting bank branches located in Ghana, Nigeria, and the United Kingdom.
A network connecting computers, printers, and servers within a school's computer laboratory.
A network connecting several telecommunications offices located across different continents.
A network connecting personal wireless earbuds to a smartphone carried by an individual.

examData.text: A telecommunications company connects several separate office networks located in different parts of the same city. Which type of network is most appropriate for describing this arrangement?
options: Personal Area Network, because the offices use computers and communication devices.
Local Area Network, because every connected office must belong to the same organization.
Metropolitan Area Network, because it connects networks across a city or large town.
Wide Area Network, because any network containing more than two computers is classified as a WAN.

examData.text: A multinational bank connects its branches across several countries so that they can exchange financial information and communicate. Which type of network is being described?
options: Personal Area Network, because the bank's employees use personal computers to access information.
Local Area Network, because the network is owned and controlled by one organization.
Metropolitan Area Network, because the bank's branches operate in different geographical locations.
Wide Area Network, because it connects computers and networks over a very large geographical area.

examData.text: Which sequence correctly arranges the four major network types from the smallest geographical coverage to the largest?
options: LAN → PAN → WAN → MAN
PAN → LAN → MAN → WAN
WAN → MAN → LAN → PAN
PAN → MAN → LAN → WAN

examData.text: Which statement best explains why the Internet is classified as a Wide Area Network in the supplied notes?
options: It connects only personal devices within a short distance using Bluetooth and USB connections.
It connects computers exclusively within one building using a common switch and Ethernet cables.
It connects networks across very large geographical areas and enables communication around the world.
It is designed to connect computers only within the boundaries of a single city or large town.

examData.text: What is meant by network topology?
options: The physical or logical arrangement of devices and connections within a computer network.
The process of converting digital signals into light signals before sending them through optical fibres.
The software used to protect computers from viruses and other forms of malicious programs.
The geographical distance between a computer and the server that supplies its requested information.

examData.text: A network has four computers connected along one main communication cable called a backbone. Which topology is being used?
options: Star topology, because every computer communicates through a central connecting device.
Ring topology, because each computer is connected to two neighbouring computers in a closed loop.
Bus topology, because all the devices connect to a single main communication cable.
Mesh topology, because every computer has a direct connection to every other computer.

examData.text: A small school wants an inexpensive network that uses less cable and is relatively simple to install. Which topology from the notes best matches these requirements?
options: Full mesh topology, because every computer requires a direct connection to every other computer.
Bus topology, because it uses a single backbone cable and is relatively inexpensive for small networks.
Tree topology, because it requires every computer to have an individual connection to a separate central server.
Hybrid topology, because combining several topologies always reduces installation and maintenance costs.

examData.text: A school uses a bus topology, but the main backbone cable develops a fault. Which consequence is most consistent with the disadvantages of this topology?
options: Only the computer nearest to the cable fault will be affected, while every other computer must continue communicating normally.
The fault will automatically cause the network to change into a star topology without any additional equipment.
The network will continue operating at a higher speed because the failure reduces the number of connected devices.
Communication across the network may be disrupted because the main cable is essential to the arrangement.

examData.text: In a computer laboratory, all computers connect to a central switch. A fault develops in one computer, but the other computers continue communicating. Which topology is being used?
options: Bus topology, because every computer depends on a single backbone cable.
Ring topology, because each computer passes data to the next computer in a closed loop.
Star topology, because each device connects to a central device and an individual computer failure usually does not affect the others.
Full mesh topology, because each computer is directly connected to every other computer in the laboratory.

examData.text: A network uses a star topology. What is the most likely result if its central switch fails?
options: Communication between connected devices may be disrupted because the central device provides their connecting point.
Only the switch itself will stop working, while all connected computers will necessarily continue communicating through it.
The network will automatically become a ring topology because the computers will establish a closed communication loop.
The failure will affect only the Internet connection, while all communication between connected computers must remain unaffected.

examData.text: Five computers are connected in a closed loop, with each computer linked to two neighbouring computers. Which topology does this represent?
options: Bus topology
Ring topology
Star topology
Tree topology

examData.text: Which statement best describes a full mesh topology?
options: Every computer connects to one central switch, which forwards information to the appropriate destination.
Every computer connects to one main cable that acts as the backbone for the entire network.
Each computer connects to two neighbouring computers to create a closed communication loop.
Every device has a direct connection to every other device, providing multiple communication paths but requiring many connections.

examData.text: An organization needs a network in which communication can continue through alternative paths if one connection fails. Which topology is most suitable according to the notes?
options: Bus topology, because all computers depend on a single communication backbone.
Star topology, because all devices depend on the same central connecting device.
Mesh topology, because it provides multiple communication paths and can remain operational when one connection fails.
Ring topology, because every device must communicate through exactly one closed-loop connection.

examData.text: A large organization connects several star networks in hierarchical levels to make expansion and management easier. Which topology is being described?
options: Tree topology
Ring topology
Bus topology
Full mesh topology

examData.text: A company combines star and bus topologies to meet its networking requirements. What is this arrangement called?
options: Personal topology
Ring topology
Tree topology
Hybrid topology

examData.text: Which networking device is designed to connect multiple devices within a LAN and forward data to the appropriate destination using network addressing information?
options: A traditional hub, which broadcasts incoming data to every connected port without making the same forwarding decisions as a modern switch.
A switch, which connects multiple devices within a LAN and forwards data to the appropriate device.
A repeater, which receives and regenerates signals to extend the distance over which communication can occur.
A modem, which performs signal conversion required by certain communication services.

examData.text: A home contains smartphones, laptops, and smart televisions that need to communicate with one another and access the Internet. Which device is commonly used to connect the home network to other networks?
options: Scanner
Repeater
Router
Printer

examData.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes a router from a switch?
options: A router connects different networks and directs data between them, while a switch connects multiple devices within a LAN.
A router displays digital information on a monitor, while a switch prints the information on paper for users.
A router stores files permanently, while a switch converts all stored information into wireless signals.
A router detects and removes viruses, while a switch verifies the identities of users before allowing access.

examData.text: Which statement best describes the operation of a traditional network hub?
options: It examines destination information and forwards data only to the specific connected device that should receive it.
It connects different networks and determines the most appropriate route for data packets.
It converts incoming network signals into light pulses for transmission through optical fibre.
It connects multiple devices and broadcasts incoming data to all connected ports.

examData.text: What is the primary function of a modem in the context of the supplied notes?
options: To provide wireless network connectivity to laptops and smartphones without requiring a physical cable.
To enable communication over certain services by converting signals between appropriate forms.
To connect every computer in a school laboratory directly to every other computer without using a switch.
To regenerate weak network signals so that they can travel beyond their normal effective range.

examData.text: A classroom has a wireless network, but the school wants to provide Wi-Fi connectivity to laptops and smartphones in another suitable area. Which device is designed to provide wireless network connectivity?
options: A network interface card that permanently stores every device's files.
A traditional hub that broadcasts all incoming data through every connected port.
A wireless access point that allows devices to connect to the network using Wi-Fi.
A modem that acts exclusively as a printer-sharing device within the school.

examData.text: A network signal becomes weak before reaching devices located farther away. Which networking device can receive and regenerate or retransmit the signal to extend communication distance?
options: Repeater
Switch
Printer
Keyboard

examData.text: Which of the following correctly describes twisted-pair cable?
options: A cable that transmits data using pulses of light through thin optical fibres.
A cable containing a central conductor surrounded by insulation and shielding, commonly used in cable television.
A cable consisting of pairs of insulated copper wires twisted together and widely used for Ethernet networks.
A wireless communication method that sends data through radio waves without requiring a physical cable.

examData.text: A school needs inexpensive network cabling that is commonly available, easy to install, and suitable for a LAN. Which transmission medium is most appropriate?
options: Satellite communication, because it does not require any physical network equipment.
Twisted-pair cable, because it is relatively inexpensive and widely used in local networks.
Fibre-optic cable, because it is always the least expensive option for every type of network installation.
Infrared transmission, because it uses insulated copper wires twisted together to carry Ethernet signals.

examData.text: Which statement best describes coaxial cable?
options: It consists of a central conductor surrounded by insulation and shielding, and it has been used in cable television and certain communication systems.
It consists of pairs of insulated copper wires twisted together and is the only cable type capable of supporting a LAN.
It transmits data using pulses of light and is completely immune to physical damage under all installation conditions.
It transmits information exclusively through wireless signals and does not contain a physical conductor.

examData.text: A telecommunications company requires a transmission medium with high data capacity, high speed, long-distance capability, and resistance to electromagnetic interference. Which medium best meets these requirements?
options: Unshielded twisted-pair cable
Coaxial cable
Wireless infrared transmission
Fibre-optic cable

examData.text: ch is a significant disadvantage of fibre-optic cable compared with many copper cables?
options: It can only transmit data over short distances and is highly susceptible to electromagnetic interference.
It requires specialized installation skills in some situations and can be more expensive than many copper cables.
It cannot transmit data at high speeds and is unsuitable for modern telecommunications networks.
It always requires more electrical power to transmit data than every other transmission medium.

examData.text: Which statement best describes wireless transmission?
options: It transmits data only through insulated copper wires connected directly between communicating devices.
It transmits data through a single backbone cable to which all devices must be connected.
It transmits data without requiring a physical cable between communicating devices, using technologies such as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
It transmits data exclusively through optical fibres and cannot support portable devices.

examData.text: A school operates a private internal website containing staff notices, administrative resources, and student records. Access is restricted to authorized members of the school. What is this network most appropriately called?
options: Internet
Extranet
Wide Area Network
Intranet

examData.text: A company allows selected external suppliers to access certain business information through a controlled private network, without giving them access to the entire internal network. Which system is being described?
options: Intranet
Extranet
Personal Area Network
Public Internet

examData.text: Which statement correctly describes a network protocol?
options: It is a physical device that connects computers and automatically provides them with electricity.
It is a storage system used to preserve data when a network connection is interrupted.
It is a set of rules that devices follow when communicating over a network so that they can exchange data correctly.
It is a computer application used exclusively to create documents and presentation slides.

examData.text: A student enters a website's domain name into a browser, and a system helps translate the name into an IP address used by the network. Which protocol-related service is responsible?
options: DNS (Domain Name System)
FTP (File Transfer Protocol)
SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)
HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol)

examData.text: Which protocol is commonly used for communication between a web browser and a web server, with its secure version using encryption to protect exchanged data?
options: SMTP and FTP
DNS and TCP/IP
FTP and SMTP
HTTP and HTTPS

examData.text: A student wants to transfer files from one computer to another over a network using a protocol specifically associated with file transfer. Which protocol should the student identify?
options: DNS
FTP
SMTP
HTTP

examData.text: Which protocol is commonly used for sending email?
options: FTP
DNS
SMTP
HTTPS

examData.text: A computer has the address 192.168.1.10. What does this address represent in the context of the notes?
options: A MAC address permanently identifying the computer's network interface at the data-link layer.
A website's domain name that must be converted into a numerical address before the browser can display a page.
An IPv4 address used for network addressing to help identify where data should be sent.
A network protocol used exclusively for transferring files between computers connected to the same LAN.

examData.text: Which statement best distinguishes an IP address from a MAC address?
options: An IP address is used for network-level addressing and routing, while a MAC address identifies a network interface at the data-link layer.
An IP address identifies a physical printer, while a MAC address determines the geographical size of a computer network.
An IP address is a protocol for sending emails, while a MAC address is a protocol for displaying websites securely.
An IP address is used only on wireless networks, while a MAC address is used only on wired networks.

examData.text: A student opens the school's online examination results system using a web browser. The computer hosting the website provides the requested page. Which statement correctly identifies the roles involved?
options: The student's browser is the server because it displays the webpage, while the school's computer is the client because it stores the files.
Both computers are servers because they are connected to the Internet and can exchange information.
The student's browser is the client because it requests the webpage, while the school's computer is the server because it provides the service.
The student's browser is a router because it directs traffic between networks, while the school's computer is a switch because it connects devices.

examData.text: Which statement correctly describes a peer-to-peer network?
options: Every computer must request all resources from a dedicated central server, which controls all communication.
Computers can communicate and share resources directly with one another without relying entirely on a dedicated central server.
Only computers belonging to different countries can exchange resources, and personal devices cannot participate.
All computers must be connected in a ring topology before they can exchange files or share resources.

examData.text: A school has many computers, and the administrator wants centralized file storage, easier backups, and better control over user access. Which network arrangement is most appropriate?
options: A peer-to-peer network in which each computer manages its own resources independently without central management.
A bus network in which all computers rely on a single backbone cable for every network function.
A personal area network in which all school computers connect directly to one student's smartphone.
A client-server network in which clients request services from centralized servers.

examData.text: A school administrator wants to protect a network against unauthorized access and attacks. Which option contains only appropriate network security measures from the notes?
options: Sharing passwords, disabling security updates, permitting unrestricted access, and avoiding backups.
Using strong passwords, authenticating users, applying firewall rules, encrypting data, controlling access, and making regular backups.
Allowing every user to access confidential files, installing unverified software, and ignoring suspicious network activity.
Removing all network devices, avoiding user authentication, and allowing unrestricted communication with unknown networks.

examData.text: A student receives a fraudulent message directing them to a fake website designed to trick them into revealing their password. Which network threat does this describe?
options: Repeater failure, because the network signal has been regenerated incorrectly.
Bandwidth congestion, because many computers are transmitting data simultaneously.
Phishing, because the message attempts to trick the user into revealing sensitive information.
Fibre-optic interference, because light signals have been disrupted during transmission.

examData.text: Students complain that video calls are delayed even though the network can carry a substantial amount of data over time. Which network performance measure is most directly concerned with the delay between sending data and receiving a response?
options: Bandwidth, because it measures the delay between a request and its response.
Network traffic, because it refers exclusively to the physical distance between two computers.
Storage capacity, because it measures how much information the network can save permanently.
Latency, because it measures the delay between sending data and receiving a response.
